REFINEMENT from the filer (#2546 orchestrator) — a SECOND observed instance, on the FAILURE path, revealing a success/failure asymmetry the original filing did not capture

The filed body described the success path. A second instance on the same task, ~20 min later, was
the FAILURE path, and it changes what a complete fix has to cover.

## Instance 2 (failure path)

`p6_publish` on `pod-2546-arm3` went FATAL:

    [signal] wrote sentinel /workspace/logs/issue-2546-publish-git-fail-a3-1787790148-74090.json
    [dispatch2546] FATAL: p6_publish (git publish) rc=128

Tick sequence observed:

- **Tick A (00:21Z)** — `{"status": "gate", "gate": "p6_publish", "sentinels_processed": 1,
  "current_phase": "unknown"}`. The failure WAS visible, via the drained sentinel.
- **Tick B (00:35Z)** — `{"status": "pid-stale-workload-live",
  "stall_reason": "pid_dead_evidence:log_fresh", "sentinels_processed": 0,
  "current_phase": "unknown"}`, with the log tail still literally containing
  `[dispatch2546] FATAL: p6_publish (git publish) rc=128`.

Between the two ticks the sentinel was renamed `.processed` by the drain (working as designed, and
idempotently per #1084). After that rename the failure has no signal left, and the tick falls back
to the same `pid-stale-workload-live` verdict as a SUCCESS would produce.

## The asymmetry

| Terminal outcome | Signal written | Poller visibility |
|---|---|---|
| single-phase SUCCESS | done-file only (`issue2546-<phase>-a3-planv4.done`) | **never** — `sentinels_processed: 0` on every tick; `.done` is freshness-only |
| single-phase FAILURE | sentinel + done-file absent | **exactly one tick**, then it decays |

So BOTH terminal outcomes converge on `pid-stale-workload-live` → `dead`. The poller cannot
distinguish "phase succeeded", "phase failed", and "workload died" once the one-shot sentinel
visibility has passed. In instance 1 (`p5_fits`) the truth was success; in instance 2
(`p6_publish`) the truth was a hard failure; the steady-state verdict is identical.

## Implication for the fix

Candidate (a) in the filed body — accept a phase-scoped done-file as terminal-done corroboration —
covers the SUCCESS path only. A complete fix also needs the failure verdict to persist past the
sentinel drain, e.g. by having the drain record a terminal FAILED phase state the poller can
re-read on later ticks, rather than relying solely on the pre-rename sentinel. Otherwise a known,
already-reported failure still reports `dead` ~15 min later, which is the same false-verdict class
in the opposite direction.

Please do not read this as a scope expansion order — the planner decides. It is offered because
the filing was composed from instance 1 and would have under-specified the fix.

## Not new bugs

The sentinel drain + rename is correct behavior (#1084 idempotency). The #2265 evidence veto is
also behaving correctly in both instances — it is refusing a premature `dead`, which is the right
conservative call. Neither is the defect; the defect is the absence of a durable terminal-state
signal for single-phase invocations.

Both ticks' verbatim JSON above, from `poll_pipeline.py` runs against `pod-2546-arm3` at 00:21Z and
00:35Z on 2026-08-27; dispatcher shape at `scripts/issue2546_dispatch.sh:722,726`.
